nodes.label: Oracle Compute Lab
nodes.rationale: Warm resource-led workbench with exactly one primary task: validate JSON source data and produce a SHA-256-bound local Morpheus compute request package for review. Deliberately scoped away from a survey-style form so the main stage shows payload shape and byte size instead of raw inputs.

nodes.label: Compute Request Package
nodes.rationale: Canonicalizes parsed JSON and emits real 64-hex SHA-256 source and request digests with no checksum fallback; one top-level request digest covers the exact returned payload plus registry snapshot rather than an unhashed self-referential digest field.

nodes.label: Network- and Route-Bound Request Digest
nodes.rationale: Binds the digest to the checked-in network and route snapshot so otherwise identical mainnet and testnet packages cannot share an identity.

nodes.label: Compute Intent Presets (risk-signal, proof-review, batch-transform)
nodes.rationale: Presets are request-planning metadata only, not separate Morpheus workflows; the single checked-in runtime workflow reference is compute.execute.

nodes.label: Keep Source Local Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: Omitting raw JSON is explicitly not encryption: the package records encryption "none" and dispatchReady false. The stage badge changes with the selected policy so the public-source option never claims the raw value stayed local.

nodes.label: Compute Runtime Dispatch Boundary
nodes.rationale: /compute/execute needs authenticated Morpheus integration and this MiniApp holds no runtime credential, so it creates no job ID and makes no network write. Because no write exists, pending/retry/readback are not_applicable; a future dispatch must persist the job ID before leaving submit and retry readback rather than re-executing.

nodes.label: Strict JSON Validation Limits (64 KB, 64-Level Nesting, Safe Integers)
nodes.rationale: Finite-number and exact-safe-integer checks prevent JSON parsing from silently changing a value before it is hashed or copied.

nodes.label: Oracle HTTP Console Generated Launcher Artwork
nodes.rationale: Banner and app mark generated with OpenAI ImageGen for a warm sunlit mint-and-gold source-to-receipt pipeline with clean foreground separation and no embedded product or network text; PNG masters preserved and hashes rechecked 2026-07-11.

nodes.label: http-oracle-pipeline.webp In-App Scene
nodes.rationale: Existing repository-owned 1672x941 source-to-extractor-to-receipt scene from commit 488fa04ec; this pass did not replace it or invent historical generation metadata.

nodes.label: Sharp WebP/AVIF Conversion Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Format-and-size conversions only; no third-party artwork enters during conversion.

nodes.label: Morpheus Oracle Health Endpoint (oracle.meshmini.app)
nodes.rationale: Health 200 is service-health evidence only; it does not prove that an arbitrary source URL, extraction path, or callback contract will succeed.

nodes.label: Testnet Service Routing Defect
nodes.rationale: The testnet health route answers with network mainnet, so testnet execution readiness cannot be claimed; routing must be corrected upstream before end-to-end testnet execution is represented as ready.

nodes.label: Dot-Separated json_path Worker Limitation
nodes.rationale: The current worker executes only a simple dot-separated json_path, not full JSONPath, so the MiniApp normalizes supported legacy notation and rejects recursive/wildcard/filter syntax instead of presenting it as ready.

nodes.label: HTTP Oracle External Execution Boundary
nodes.rationale: No runtime credential, callback contract, callback method, wallet action or transaction path exists in this MiniApp; those belong to the separate callback-binding workflow.

nodes.label: Oracle HTTP Console Release 1.2.0
nodes.rationale: Accepted build is byte-identical to the host public MiniApp directory; catalog stays 77/77 unique app IDs and slugs with one Oracle HTTP Console entry.

nodes.label: Draft Digest Invalidation On Edit
nodes.rationale: Editing any prepared input invalidates both the visible receipt and the host shell digest until the user prepares again, so a copied payload always matches its digest.

nodes.label: Shared Preview Kernel Endpoint Validation
nodes.rationale: Public endpoints are validated consistently by both the visual surface and the shared preview kernel so the two surfaces cannot disagree about what is acceptable.

nodes.label: Shared Generated Morpheus Registry
nodes.rationale: Single generated source of network/route/contract truth that each Oracle console resolves the selected launch network through, instead of embedding per-app static endpoints.

nodes.label: Oracle HTTP Console
nodes.rationale: Visual payload builder for Morpheus HTTP oracle intents: a source-to-extractor-to-draft-package pipeline is the first screen while exact request fields stay in a compact Details drawer. It builds, validates, hashes and copies locally and never fetches, binds a callback, or submits.

nodes.label: MorpheusHttpPayload
nodes.rationale: Uses the real json_path, target_chain, URL, method, JSON-header and body field names expected by the worker; GET omits the body and POST preserves the exact bytes of at most 32 KiB of valid JSON in both digest and copy.

nodes.label: JSONPath Normalization to Runtime Dot Path
nodes.rationale: Familiar $.data[0].price input is normalized to data.0.price so users can type the notation they know without the app implying unsupported JSONPath features will run.

nodes.label: Public Source URL Validation Policy
nodes.rationale: Credentials, URL fragments, local hosts and literal private-network addresses are rejected because the remote oracle lane cannot use them as entered; final DNS resolution and endpoint policy still happen in Morpheus at execution time.

nodes.label: Network-Bound SHA-256 Draft Digest
nodes.rationale: Identifies this local network + route + payload draft only. It is explicitly not a worker signature, callback receipt, or proof that the oracle ran.

nodes.label: Separate Callback-Binding Workflow
nodes.rationale: Actual oracle execution starts only when this separate workflow submits the copied payload, which keeps the console free of wallet and blockchain permissions.

nodes.label: oracle-workspace-stage.webp Workspace Artwork
nodes.rationale: Repository-owned artwork added in commit 488fa04ec, referenced directly without stretching or an artificial overlay; original generation metadata is not present beside the file so no stronger authorship claim is made.

nodes.label: Identity Evidence-Pass Launcher Mark
nodes.rationale: Depicts an identity evidence card passing through an inspection lens and deliberately avoids a shield, lock, checkmark, token mark or text, so the icon itself cannot imply identity was verified.

nodes.label: Retired OneGate/NEP-21 Banner Assets
nodes.rationale: Older banner carries stale OneGate / NEP-21 / Testnet labels and is no longer referenced by manifest or Open Graph metadata; legacy variants stay packaged only for compatibility.

nodes.label: NeoDIDRegistry Contract 0xb81f31ea81e279793b30411b82c2e82078b63105
nodes.rationale: Canonical Neo N3 mainnet anchor checked with read-only RPC alongside network magic 860833102 and manifest name NeoDIDRegistry; a verified deployment observation still is not identity or claim verification.

nodes.label: Testnet no-network-deployment Evidence
nodes.rationale: Emitted only after RPC network magic 894710606 is confirmed; an unexpected resolver anchor on testnet is reported as a mismatch rather than a deployment.

nodes.label: Same-Origin NeoDID Resolver and Provider Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Host exposes /api/morpheus/neodid/resolve and /api/morpheus/neodid/providers accepting Morpheus service, Vault and AA identifiers; provider responses carry no explicit network or source fields so the app never invents those upstream claims.

nodes.label: MorpheusOracleGateway DID Service Declaration
nodes.rationale: Presence in a DID service list means an endpoint is declared; it does not prove an Oracle request ran.

nodes.label: Metadata-Only Evidence Boundary
nodes.rationale: A resolver response is not subject-to-wallet binding and a provider/claim catalog match is metadata only; payload structure is strictly decoded before it can become evidence, and no wallet, signature, transaction, deployment, funded account or secret is used.

nodes.label: Oracle NeoDID Console Release 2.1.0
nodes.rationale: 41/41 focused tests, byte-identical host copy, and a 77/77 catalog; no deployment, browser session, wallet, signature or transaction was performed.

nodes.label: Digest-Checked, Network-Isolated Expiring Evidence
nodes.rationale: Results are SHA-256 digest checked, network isolated, short lived, recoverable after interrupted safe reads, and cleared before every retry or failure; copy performs an independent expiry gate so the UI refresh interval cannot leak a stale snapshot.

nodes.label: Storage Write/Delete Readback Requirement
nodes.rationale: Storage availability is advertised only after write and delete readback succeed, so silent storage no-ops cannot produce a false recovery promise.

nodes.label: Bounded Structural Payload Decoding
nodes.rationale: Resolver and provider payloads decode as bounded structures and ambiguous provider aliases are rejected instead of silently selecting a record; malformed payloads degrade to unavailable rather than being filtered into evidence.

nodes.label: Oracle NeoDID Console
nodes.rationale: Read-only evidence inspector for Morpheus NeoDID: resolves a supported DID, reads the launched network's provider catalog, and checks the resolver-declared registry anchor against the canonical Neo deployment.

nodes.label: Resolve DID Primary Action
nodes.rationale: Inspects the default NeoDID service identifier immediately so the first screen produces evidence without requiring the user to open the exact-identifier drawer.

nodes.label: Fifteen-Minute Evidence Expiry
nodes.rationale: Latest result expires after fifteen minutes even while the app stays open; an interrupted resolver GET can be resumed for five minutes and failures clear the prior snapshot before surfacing an error.

nodes.label: Non-Verification Product Boundary
nodes.rationale: Does not verify identity, attest a claim, verify a signature, dispatch an Oracle job, connect a wallet, or broadcast a transaction; identity verification, claim attestation, signature verification and Oracle dispatch are recorded as not-performed in every export.

nodes.label: Oracle NeoDID Console (Simplified Chinese README)
nodes.rationale: Localized mirror of the English README preserving the same non-verification boundary language, contract identifiers, and expiry semantics so the bilingual product copy cannot diverge in what it claims.

nodes.label: Oracle NeoDID Console HTML Entry
nodes.rationale: Declares the description meta as inspecting resolver, provider catalog and registry evidence without claiming identity verification, matching the README boundary.

nodes.label: oracle-market-stage.webp Market Stage
nodes.rationale: Generated 2026-07-11 with a centered price prism and candlestick surface that works in both the in-app crop and the wide catalog treatment without introducing fake token marks.

nodes.label: Shared CoinArt Token Artwork Component
nodes.rationale: NEO and GAS identity is rendered separately through the centrally maintained shared component sourced from the Neo press-kit pipeline, so the generated raster never doubles as token identity.

nodes.label: Retired Price Console Launcher Assets
nodes.rationale: banner.webp/avif/svg and logo.svg contain stale OneGate / NEP-21 / Testnet labels and are retained only for compatibility; active manifest and Open Graph metadata use the generated market stage and WebP mark.

nodes.label: Morpheus DataFeed Contracts (mainnet 0x03013f49, testnet 0x9bea75cf)
nodes.rationale: Network-specific RPC/contract pairs bound from the generated Morpheus registry; the production MiniApp uses the same pairs that read-only verification exercised.

nodes.label: getLatest(String) Read-Only Contract Call
nodes.rationale: Called directly against each configured DataFeed contract with no wallet, signature or transaction; returns the fixed six-decimal integer scale used by both price display and the secondary route reference.

nodes.label: On-Chain Write vs Upstream Source Timestamp Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Exposing on-chain write freshness and upstream market-source time separately stops a recently rewritten record from hiding an old market source, keeping the stale testnet GAS record visibly stale.

nodes.label: AGG/TWELVEDATA Feed Key Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Resolves the canonical AGG:<ASSET>-USD key first and falls back to the exact TWELVEDATA:<ASSET>-USD key only explicitly, exposing the resolved key so a provider fallback is never mistaken for the aggregate.

nodes.label: Oracle Price Console Release 1.1.0
nodes.rationale: 34 tests across 3 files, 17/17 emitted files served 200, 9/9 public assets byte-identical, and a 77/77 catalog; visual interaction review is explicitly left to a separate browser pass.

nodes.label: Per-Network Manifest DataFeed Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Declaring network-specific DataFeed dependencies in the public manifest prevents a static mainnet-only stateSource from misdescribing a testnet launch.

nodes.label: Six-Decimal Price Scale Parsing
nodes.rationale: Rejects strings, non-finite values, unsafe values and anything that cannot map back to the contract's integer scale, so small positive prices never collapse into a misleading $0.0000.

nodes.label: Pair/Request Generation Guard
nodes.rationale: Generation counters stop stale catalog or quote responses from taking ownership after a newer selection or teardown, so a late NEO response cannot overwrite a newer GAS selection.

nodes.label: Oracle Price Console
nodes.rationale: Timestamp-bound Morpheus market signal station for Neo N3; the price ticket, official NEO/GAS assets, freshness and request path lead while raw request parameters stay off the first screen. Read-only: it never signs transactions or claims a data-feed read is a trade.

nodes.label: One-Hour Freshness Boundary Signal
nodes.rationale: Uses the on-chain record timestamp as the freshness signal; missing or implausibly future timestamps stay explicitly unverified and a once-fresh quote becomes stale at the one-hour boundary without another request.

nodes.label: Launch Link Pair Normalization
nodes.rationale: Accepts a bare symbol, a USD pair, or the exact resolved aggregate/provider key, and rejects another quote currency instead of silently relabeling it as USD.

nodes.label: On-Chain Pair Catalog Progressive Enhancement
nodes.rationale: Catalog failure leaves the stable NEO/GAS/BTC watchlist available, and only bounded USD pairs are normalized while malformed or cross-quote entries are ignored.

nodes.label: seal-reference-stage.webp Seal Chamber
nodes.rationale: Existing repository asset from commit 488fa04ec reused because the app already contained a suitable bright product-specific seal-chamber resource; no new image was generated and original provider metadata is not claimed.

nodes.label: Sharp Centered-Crop Launcher Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Banner and icon are deterministic centered cover resizes and a 700x700 envelope crop of the seal chamber, so launcher art and in-app art cannot drift into two identities.

nodes.label: Removed Handcrafted SVG Launchers
nodes.rationale: The older handcrafted banner.svg and logo.svg were deleted so the build does not package a second inconsistent visual identity.

nodes.label: MorpheusOracle Contract (mainnet 0xf54d8584, testnet 0x4b882e94)
nodes.rationale: Read directly from canonical N3Index RPC via getcontractstate, oracleEncryptionPublicKey and oracleEncryptionAlgorithm so verifying the Oracle contract does not depend on an installed wallet provider; both batches returned HALT with matching MorpheusOracle manifests.

nodes.label: Oracle Public-Key Route (/api/morpheus/oracle/public-key)
nodes.rationale: Per-network key/algorithm response cross-checked against the direct contract read; the app compares the platform response with an independent RPC read rather than trusting either alone.

nodes.label: Confidential Store Host Proxy Route
nodes.rationale: Answers opaque-frame preflight, exposes a non-mutating per-network capability response, and forwards ciphertext only when server-side store token and project slug are configured; the credential is added only server-to-server and the project slug cannot be supplied by the MiniApp.

nodes.label: secret_ref Routing-Receipt Boundary
nodes.rationale: The route exposes no ciphertext readback contract, so the frontend treats secret_ref only as a service routing receipt and explicitly not as ownership, retrieval proof, a transaction, confidential execution, or attestation.

nodes.label: Opaque-Origin CORS Deployment Gate
nodes.rationale: Deployed neomini.app responses still lack Access-Control-Allow-Origin and use a revalidating cache policy while the checked-in route sets wildcard CORS and no-store, so the deployed route is behind source and remains a release gate for opaque-origin MiniApp execution.

nodes.label: Oracle Seal Console Release Condition
nodes.rationale: Frontend, local protocol, host transport and error recovery are release-candidate complete in source, but external enablement stays conditional on deploying the public-key/store routes with server-only configuration and executing one authorized non-sensitive store/receipt lifecycle. Until the read-only capability reports ready, new encryption stays disabled.

nodes.label: Cross-Action Coordinator
nodes.rationale: One coordinator joins duplicate readiness reads and rejects conflicting seal/retry/cleanup actions so races cannot produce stale observable results; rejected promises are consumed after the shared status layer reports failure to avoid unhandled browser rejections.

nodes.label: Ciphertext Recovery Journal
nodes.rationale: Exact ciphertext is saved before the first external store request and a dropped journal prevents that request entirely; a returned receipt is journaled as stored before cleanup so interrupted cleanup becomes a local-only finalization instead of a second POST. Receipts are deduplicated by fingerprint and capped at eight device-local records.

nodes.label: 64 KiB Plaintext / 64-Level Nesting Validation
nodes.rationale: Non-empty JSON object, 64 KiB plaintext, 64-level nesting, finite/safe numeric values, 256 KiB ciphertext envelope, route-length, safe-timestamp and exact-reference validation gate every seal.

nodes.label: PlayStage + OpenUiLite Design System
nodes.rationale: Shared shell hosting the warm resource-led seal studio; the generic platform operation form stays empty so the native workbench is the only interaction surface.

nodes.label: Oracle Seal Console
nodes.rationale: Confidential-payload workbench for Neo N3 and the Morpheus Oracle seal lane; one visible prepare-seal-receipt journey on the main stage with route, JSON editor, full receipt and diagnostics in a detail drawer. No wallet connection, signature, token amount, fee, or on-chain transaction path exists.

nodes.label: Nine-Step Seal Product Path
nodes.rationale: Validate JSON, require working recovery storage, fetch a fresh network-specific X25519 key, require a configured store capability, independently verify the contract by RPC, encrypt locally, persist and verify the ciphertext before the first request, accept only a valid non-zero reference, then mark the journal stored before cleanup.

nodes.label: X25519-HKDF-SHA256-AES-256-GCM Encryption
nodes.rationale: Pinned algorithm with a raw 32-byte X25519 endpoint key; encryption happens browser-locally before anything leaves the device.

nodes.label: Framework-v2 Ciphertext Envelope
nodes.rationale: Recovery accepts only the exact six-field envelope plus its real SHA-256 fingerprint, public routing metadata, network/contract identity and retry state; injected plaintext or unknown fields cannot enter a retry and source JSON never leaves React component state.

nodes.label: Same-Origin Confidential-Store Capability Check
nodes.rationale: A read-only GET must confirm the server-side store credential and project binding for the exact selected network before any new plaintext is encrypted, so the app never produces ciphertext it cannot deliver.

nodes.label: VRF-Graded oracle-workspace-stage.webp
nodes.rationale: Cool white-balance grade, violet corner vignette and violet accent bar derived from the shared Oracle workspace render so the VRF stage is visually distinct from the warm NeoDID original kept verbatim, satisfying unique-banner-content checks.

nodes.label: scripts/generate-workspace-stage.mjs
nodes.rationale: Sharp-based generator that derives the VRF-graded stage deterministically from the shared base render instead of hand-editing a copy.

nodes.label: audit:miniapps:media Unique-Banner Content Check
nodes.rationale: Repository media audit that forbids two MiniApps from shipping the same banner content, forcing per-app grading of shared base renders.

nodes.label: Upstream Authorship/License Provenance Gap
nodes.rationale: Git history proves when the files entered the repository but not their upstream authorship or license; that record must be resolved before redistributing the art outside this repository or into a separately licensed bundle.
